text:
olga: FYI ran a mixed-model canary (ndjson streaming) after the orca-lite fixes. We're seeing sporadic NDJSON parse failures where the model emits fenced blocks or explanatory text after the object. attaching a sample.
ryan: paste the raw snippet?
olga: here's a representative one (from the stream):
```
```json
{"tool":"profile_enrich","args":{"id":"acct_42","attrs":["plan","signup_ts"]}}
```

Note: the stream then continues with another JSON object on the next line. Our NDJSON reader chokes on the fence.
nikhil: canary-bot stats?
canary-bot: Run 1789999000: schema_fail_rate=0.27% (baseline=0.09%), parse_err_count=187, affected_variants=[orca-lite-int8, kestrel-int4], streaming_mode=ndjson
ryan: two pragmatic mitigations: 1) conservative sanitizer that strips ```json fences only when the inner text is valid JSON 2) length-prefixed JSON: model emits a single line marker like </s>__JL__LEN=NNN then exactly NNN bytes of JSON. Parser reads NNN bytes and ignores fences.
nikhil: length-pref looks robust for streaming chunk boundaries, less brittle than sentinel tokens that can be generated. But must ensure tokenizers don't split the marker. We should pick a closed-vocab prefix like `</s>__JL__LEN=` and validate per-tokenizer.
olga: did a quick experiment: injected `</s>__JL__LEN=123` on its own line before the JSON for orca-lite-int8 only. Result: schema_fail_rate dropped 0.27% -> 0.06%, collisions=0.0003%. Logged collision/noise samples to s3://redwood-canaries/ndjson/1789999000/lenpref-examples.ndjson
ryan: nice. Any adverse effects (data loss, misalignment)?
olga: small edge: when model emits extra whitespace lines after JSON but before next object, our reader still handles it. The bigger risk is if the model lies about NNN (rare) or emits utf-8 multi-byte sequences and we miscount bytes vs codepoints. Parser must count raw bytes.
nikhil: implement token-safety scan across tokenizers to confirm `</s>__JL__LEN=` is not sub-tokenized. I'll run this across zephyr/sable/orca/kestrel.
ryan: short-term plan: enable len-pref parsing in canary for streaming-ndjson only (owner=olga). Add golden-set validation after parse (required keys + type checks). If golden-set fails, auto-retry with batch=1 token_cutoff+=128.
infra-bot: noted. mid-term: add tokenizer-safety report and fallback sentinel candidates list (owner=nikhil). long-term: runtime should produce chunk outputs aligned to token boundaries and expose a canary mode to prefer byte-aligned streaming.
olga: I'll flip the canary flag and add dashboard panels for lenpref acceptance_rate and golden-set rejects. PR incoming.
ryan: also add a parser-mode: lenpref-first, sanitizer-second, heal-json-last. Keeps behavior deterministic.
nikhil: one more thought: for NDJSON we should treat fenced code as a signal rather than an error. If fence detected and inner content valid, accept it. Lenpref covers the rest.
olga: agreed. deploying now. Will report back after 6h canary. :thumbsup:
